primary_evidence.note: The official product page explicitly names Geotrek-admin and describes it as the back-office application for managing trails, places, and tourism information; it also links the source and identifies the BSD license. The 100+ figure is suite-level and is not attributed solely to this repository.

product_identity: Geotrek-admin, the Geotrek suite’s back-office application for managing trails, treks, points of interest, interventions, and tourism data
agency: Parc national des Écrins and Parc national du Mercantour (public project commissioners; the broader Geotrek community includes additional public land managers)
geography: France (French national parks; Geotrek also has an Italian park partner)
family_note: Geotrek-admin is the core management back-office, distinct from Geotrek-rando, Geotrek-widget, and Geotrek-mobile. Do not count those suite components or per-organization instances as separate Geotrek-admin products; the 100+ deployment figure is for Geotrek at suite/application level.
status_note: The project history dates Geotrek’s beginnings to 2012, but the first located public-version commit that adds the BSD-2-Clause LICENSE is 2013-05-07: https://github.com/GeotrekCE/Geotrek-admin/commit/b96d7aeb82e75c38397422d7b224f9722b2e6b50. The 2014 PNE procurement specification corroborates a 2012/2013 development period and BSD release on a forge. Therefore 2013 is used for first defensible public licensed source, not the earlier project origin. The official current product page identifies this repository’s back-office scope; no suite-wide license claim is made.

decision_reason: The assigned repository is the public G’MIC interpreter/library and command-line framework, with upstream download, build, and usage documentation. It is an independently usable operational image-processing tool developed within a French public research unit; the project maintains current releases and extensive documentation. This record does not transfer the core repo’s license to separately hosted G’MIC-Qt or community-filter repositories.

government_provenance.note: GREYC’s October 2021 news explicitly says G’MIC is developed in its IMAGE team; GREYC’s laboratory page identifies the unit’s cotutelles as CNRS, UNICAEN, and ENSICAEN: https://www.greyc.fr/laboratoire/. The linked GreycLab GitHub repository is the official public source for the scoped core product.

public_source.note: The public repository contains C++ source, build materials, tests, license texts, and project history; the official download page links it as the G’MIC-core source repository.

eligible_license.note: The official 2.1.9 source archive (2018-01-19) and its core notices cover files such as src/gmic.cpp, src/gmic.h, src/gmic_cli.cpp, src/gmic_stdlib.h, and src/CImg.h with a per-file choice of CeCILL-C or CeCILL v2.1; CeCILL 2.1 is the OSI-approved option. This is a file-scoped dual grant, not one blanket repository expression. The separately sourced optional libcgmic C API bridge in G’MIC-community has a CeCILL-B notice and is excluded from this product/license scope.

primary_evidence.note: The official download page links the G’MIC-core public repository, stable source tarballs, platform packages, and explicit Debian/Ubuntu and Windows build instructions for the core command-line tool and C++ library. The separately sourced optional libcgmic C API bridge and other G’MIC repositories are outside this record’s scope.

product_identity: G’MIC core C++ interpreter/library and command-line image-processing framework (the assigned `gmic` repository; excludes separately sourced C API bridge and other repositories)
agency: GREYC UMR CNRS 6072 / IMAGE team (joint research unit under CNRS, ENSICAEN, and the University of Caen Normandie)
license: Per-file choice of CeCILL-C or CeCILL v2.1 for the scoped core C++/CLI files; CeCILL 2.1 is OSI-approved. Separate repositories/bridge excluded.
family_note: Keep this record scoped to the core interpreter/library/CLI repository. G’MIC-Qt and G’MIC-community are separate repositories. In particular, the optional libcgmic C API bridge is separately sourced from G’MIC-community and uses CeCILL-B; it is excluded from this core product record. Do not extend the core license claim to other repositories or filter assets.
status_note: The official source archive index https://gmic.eu/files/source/ dates gmic_2.1.9.tar.gz to 2018-01-19. Its core file notices state a per-file choice of CeCILL-C or CeCILL v2.1, making 2018 the earliest located eligible-grant source year. Checked earlier source archives through 2.1.8 (2018-01-02), including 2.1.7 (2017-12-21) and earlier sampled releases; those inspected notices remained CeCILL v2.0. The project’s 2008 origin predates this verified OSI-eligible option. The scoped product is the core C++ interpreter/library and CLI. The optional libcgmic C API bridge is fetched from the separate G’MIC-community repository and has a CeCILL-B notice; it is excluded, as are G’MIC-Qt and community filters.

decision_reason: The public IGN SDK provides documented, versioned 2D/3D JavaScript mapping functionality, but its material SDK code is CeCILL-B-only. Because CeCILL-B is not OSI-approved and third-party dependency licenses do not grant the SDK code, it is ineligible under the review methodology.

government_provenance.note: The exact repository README says this is the Web Géoplateforme SDK made available by IGN. The IGNF organization is the verified account of the National Institute of Geographic and Forest Information; IGN’s official identity card identifies it as a public administrative establishment under ministry authority: https://www.ign.fr/institut/identity-card.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains 2D and 3D JavaScript code, samples, source documentation, and compile/setup guidance without access restrictions.

eligible_license.note: The SDK’s own 2D and 3D notices both grant CeCILL-B: https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/blob/develop/LICENCE-2D.md and https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/blob/develop/LICENCE-3D.md. OSI’s approved-license list includes CeCILL-2.1 but not CeCILL-B: https://opensource.org/licenses. Third-party components retain their own grants and do not license the SDK code. No eligible alternate grant for the material SDK code was found.

primary_evidence.note: The exact repository publishes the SDK as a reusable product; the release page documents version 3.5.6 (12 June 2025), while the repository README links installation/use guides for both 2D and 3D variants.

product_identity: IGN Web Géoplateforme SDK (historically Geoportal SDK), a JavaScript library for integrating Géoplateforme resources into websites in 2D or 3D
agency: Institut national de l’information géographique et forestière (IGN)
license: CeCILL-B for the SDK code; no OSI-approved alternate grant located
family_note: The 2D and 3D SDK variants are maintained in this same product repository and should not be counted as separate products. OpenLayers, iTowns, and other bundled third-party components retain separate license terms.
status_note: The 2016-12-07 initial SDK commit added source together with a CeCILL-B notice: https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/commit/730598b6f3e05135a9d224cb5cdd18c7ac5bcac8. Current 2D and 3D notices continue to license SDK code under CeCILL-B. OSI’s current approved list includes CeCILL-2.1 but not CeCILL-B, so the SDK fails eligible-license review; third-party library grants do not change that result.

decision_reason: xan is a substantially rewritten, actively distributed CSV command-line tool developed by Sciences Po’s médialab for the lab’s daily research/data workflows. It has comprehensive user documentation, multiple installation channels, and versioned binary releases. The source is public and dual-licensed under Unlicense or MIT; agency attribution is to the IEP de Paris public institution through its médialab research unit, with the private FNSP governance nuance recorded.

government_provenance.note: The Ministry’s research-structure register identifies médialab as a Sciences Po research unit and lists the IEP de Paris/FNSP establishment. IEP de Paris is legally a public EPCSCP, although it is managed by the separate private FNSP: https://www.sciencespo.fr/en/legal-terms/. The exact official product page says xan was forked, substantially rewritten, and adapted by the lab for its daily use.

public_source.note: The repository is public and contains the Rust source, tests, extensive user reference, install guides, and release assets.

eligible_license.note: The public repository includes UNLICENSE and LICENSE-MIT; its licensing and Cargo metadata present the product as Unlicense OR MIT, allowing users to select either eligible grant. The current MIT grant is at https://github.com/medialab/xan/blob/master/LICENSE-MIT. Earlier 2015 grant history is imported xsv history and is not used to date xan.

primary_evidence.note: The official product page identifies xan by name, links the exact source repo, describes the CSV-processing command-line tool, and says the lab extensively rewrote it for daily use. The repo’s current README documents installation through Cargo and package managers, command/reference docs, and prebuilt releases.

product_identity: xan, a Rust command-line tool for processing, querying, and visualizing large CSV and related tabular datasets
agency: Médialab research unit of the Institut d’études politiques de Paris (IEP de Paris, a public EPCSCP; IEP is managed within the dual Sciences Po structure by the private FNSP)
license: Unlicense OR MIT (dual-licensed; user may choose either grant)
family_note: xan began as a fork of xsv but its official product page says the médialab extensively rewrote and expanded it for its own research/data-collection workflows. Count xan as this distinct product, not as the upstream xsv or the entire médialab software portfolio.
status_note: GitHub records this repository’s creation on 2018-07-10. A substantive xan-specific source change to src/config.rs is publicly recorded in the repository on 2018-07-11: https://github.com/medialab/xan/commit/bf799a5090d7cbd313e1d7cd15853f02e68340a0; the repository includes the Unlicense and MIT grants. The 2015 license commit in imported history belongs to upstream BurntSushi/xsv and is not treated as evidence that xan itself was public then. The official product page verifies the current product identity and lab use; current releases establish ongoing distribution. Sciences Po’s legal terms distinguish the public IEP from the private FNSP that manages it.

decision_reason: Government sponsorship, public source, MIT licensing, and a 2021 source/license year are supported. However, the exact official evidence describes Jitsi Box as a prototype and “message in a bottle” inviting teachers to test it, with a more complete product conditional on demand. The 2022 classroom experiment is real but appears to be pilot-stage rather than independent reuse, a production operational tool, or a versioned agency-published product; hold pending evidence of subsequent deployment/reuse or a maintained versioned distribution.

government_provenance.note: The official FUN announcement states that France Université Numérique and CentraleSupélec’s Digital Lab developed this exact Jitsi Box prototype. FUN’s official About page identifies France Université Numérique as a GIP: https://www.fun-mooc.fr/fr/a-propos/.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the React application, Raspberry Pi controller materials, setup guidance, and no-access-barrier source code.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an actual MIT license and the README states the work is released under the MIT License. Git history shows the license was added on 2021-11-29 (https://github.com/openfun/jitsi-box/commit/bd539bdf4424e350abece77ef47d53368b59d59e).

primary_evidence.note: The exact official announcement calls this a first operational prototype and explicitly frames it as a call for teacher adoption before a more advanced version could be made. A later official account reports classroom experiments in several Vosges collèges (https://www.fun-mooc.fr/fr/actualites/retour-sur-les-experimentations-de-la-jitsi-box-en-classe/), but I found no evidence that the source became a maintained production tool, independently reused deployment, or versioned product release. Pilot activity plus a DIY setup guide alone does not clear the notability baseline.

product_identity: Jitsi Box, a Raspberry Pi/touchscreen classroom hybrid-conferencing prototype built around Jitsi
agency: France Université Numérique (GIP) and CentraleSupélec Digital Lab
family_note: Jitsi Box is a bespoke hybrid-classroom device/app integrating the separate Jitsi meeting system; do not count upstream Jitsi or the hosted demo as part of this repository’s product/license scope.
status_note: Functional source appears in the repository from November 2021 and the MIT grant was added on 2021-11-29. Official evidence documents a pilot and conference demonstrations in 2022, but not post-pilot adoption or current maintenance. Clear this hold with exact evidence of a versioned release plus installation/user guidance, sustained operational use, or independent reuse.
